newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power mixed amid line outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power mixed amid line outage.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished mixed Monday amid outage of a high-voltage transmission line that moves power from western to central and southern New York state.

The outage of the line, operated by Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, reduced normal capacity of the so called "Central-East Interface" by 1,000 megawatt (MW). The transfer point usually has a capacity of 2,600-2,700 MW.
"That cut some schedules today at Central-East," said a New York trader.
The maintenance shutdown of the 345 kilovolt (KV) line, which runs between Utica and Albany, began today and was planned to stay down until Friday.

Because of reduced capability to import from the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP), prices in eastern NYPP spiked up today as utilities tried to switch on expensive oil and natural gas-fired generation, market sources said.
In the eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday rose to $31.00-$33.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from Friday's $28.00-$29.00 range for Monday delivery.
Off-peak, non-firm power for Tuesday in eastern NYPP was quoted at $19.00-$20.00, higher than Friday's $18.50-$19.00.

In the western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday slipped to $19.00-$20.00, off sharply from Friday's quote of $22.00-$25.00 as a result of greater supply in the western part of the grid due to the transmission constraint.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Tuesday held steady at $14.00-$15.00.
Spot power prices in the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), moved higher in sympathy in eastern NYPP tied to the line restriction.
Peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at the Northeast Utilities border was quoted at $35.00-$36.00, up from Friday's $33.00-$35.00 range for Monday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Tuesday delivery to the NU border was quoted at $21.00-$22.00, up from Friday's $21.00.
Vermont Yankee Power Corp trimmed output at its 510 MW Vermont Yankee plant to 80 percent of capacity while repairing a condensate pump seal leak.

Tuesday's temperatures in the Northeast were predicted to peak in 40s Fahrenheit and bottom in the 20s-30s. A cooling trend was forecast Friday with temperaturees falling to two to four degrees below normal
